Question_text: A student investigates how the current in a thermistor depends upon temperature. She sets up the circuit shown in Fig. 1.1. She pours hot water into the beaker. She stirs the water, measures its temperature and reads the ammeter. She records the values of temperature and current in the table of Fig. 1.2. She repeats these readings at 10°C intervals, as the water cools, until the water reaches room temperature. She records all her readings in the table, as shown in Fig. 1.2. Table of Fig. 1.2: temperature θ/°C | current I/mA ------------------|------------- 80 | 2.90 70 | 2.30 60 | 1.75 50 | 1.20 40 | (missing value) 30 | 0.60 20 | 0.45
image: Fig. 1.1 shows a circuit diagram. A 5.0 V power supply is connected in series with a milliammeter and a thermistor. The thermistor is immersed in water within a beaker, along with a thermometer. The water in the beaker is shown being stirred. The text 'thermometer', 'water', 'milliammeter', and 'thermistor' are labeled on the diagram, and the power supply is labeled '5.0 V' with a 'mA' symbol for the milliammeter.

Parts.part_text: Read the ammeter and record the missing value of current in the table of Fig. 1.2.
Parts.image: Fig. 1.3 shows an analog milliammeter with a circular scale ranging from 0 to 3 mA. Major divisions are marked at 0.5, 1, 1.5, 2, 2.5, and 3 mA, with smaller divisions indicating 0.1 mA increments. The needle is pointing at 0.9 mA, which is four small divisions past 0.5 mA.

Parts.part_text: State why the student stirs the water before taking a temperature reading.
On Fig. 1.4, plot a graph of I on the y-axis against θ on the x-axis. Start both axes from the origin. Draw the smooth curve of best fit.
Parts.image: Fig. 1.4 shows a blank grid with both x and y axes starting from 0, ready for plotting data points and drawing a graph. The y-axis is intended for current (I) and the x-axis for temperature (θ).

Parts.part_text: Extend your curve to predict the current for the temperature of 0°C. current at 0°C = ......................................mA
Suggest how the student can modify her investigation to check the prediction made in (c)(i).
Use your graph to estimate the current I when the temperature of the water is 75°C. I = ......................................mA
The voltage V of the power supply is 5.0 V. Use the equation R = V/I to calculate the resistance R of the thermistor at 75 °C. R = ......................................Ω
Describe the relationship between current and temperature for the thermistor, shown by your graph.
Deduce the relationship between resistance and temperature for the thermistor.

Question_text: A student measures the focal length of a convex lens. He sets up the apparatus shown in Fig. 2.1. He places the lens a distance from the illuminated object. He moves the screen until a sharp image of the object is formed on the screen.
image: Fig. 2.1 shows an optical bench setup. From left to right: a lamp (labeled 'illuminated object'), a convex lens in a holder, and a screen. The distance from the lamp (object) to the lens is labeled 'x', and the distance from the lens to the screen (image) is labeled 'y'. The diagram includes a note indicating it is 'one-eighth full size'.

Parts.part_text: Measure, to the nearest millimetre, the length x and the length y on Fig. 2.1.
The diagram in Fig. 2.1 is drawn one-eighth full size. Calculate the distance u from the object to the lens and the distance v from the image to the lens.
Calculate the focal length f of the lens, using the equation f = uv / (u + v). Give your answer to 2 significant figures.
State one precaution that the student takes to obtain an accurate value for the focal length f of the lens.

Question_text: A student and her friend measure an approximate value for the speed of sound in air using echoes. She stands a large distance from a reflecting wall. She claps her hands at a regular rate. She adjusts her rate of clapping until each clap coincides with the echo of the previous clap. Her friend then uses a stopwatch to measure the time t between claps. They measure the distance to the wall. The time t between claps is recorded four times. The values of t, measured in seconds, are shown below. 0.87, 0.97, 0.94, 0.88

Parts.part_text: Calculate t_av, the average value of t. Give your answer to 2 decimal places.
Suggest why it is sensible to give t_av to 2 decimal places.
The distance s from the students to the wall is 130 m. A metre rule is not an appropriate device for measuring this distance. Suggest a device that can be used to measure this distance.
The speed v of sound in air is given by the equation v = 2s / t_av. Calculate v.
Suggest one reason why the value for the speed of sound in air measured by this method is only approximate.

Question_text: A student uses a plotting compass to plot the pattern of the magnetic field between the North poles of two bar magnets. The student places the magnets on a sheet of white paper, as shown in Fig. 4.1.
image: Fig. 4.1 shows two bar magnets placed on a sheet of white paper. They are arranged horizontally with their North poles facing each other, separated by a gap. The North pole of the left magnet is labeled 'N', and its South pole 'S'. The North pole of the right magnet is labeled 'N', and its South pole 'S'. A small plotting compass is depicted near the North pole of the right magnet, with an arrow indicating its North direction. This setup is for plotting a magnetic field.

Parts.part_text: Describe how the student uses the plotting compass to plot the pattern of the magnetic field. You may add to Fig. 4.1 to help you explain your answer, if you wish.
State what else the student can deduce about the magnetic field in this investigation.
